standard_prerequisites.name: A filtered colimit of valuation rings with compatible value groups is a valuation ring, and the value group of the colimit is computed from the colimit of the value groups

core_obligations: Write the henselization as the filtered colimit of the localizations of etale algebras at primes lying over the maximal ideal of the valuation ring, using the standard description (proof lines 37545-37549).

Apply the statement on etale extensions of valuation rings to each term of the colimit to see that each localization is a valuation ring and that the induced map on value groups is bijective (proof lines 37549-37556).

Use the statement on filtered colimits of valuation rings to conclude that the henselization is a valuation ring and that the map on value groups from the ring to its henselization is bijective, which proves the lemma for the first inclusion (proof lines 37556-37561).

Repeat the same argument with the strict henselization in place of the henselization, and use that the strict henselization of the henselization is the strict henselization of the ring to obtain the remaining two inclusions, which completes the proof (proof lines 37562-37565).
proof_roadmap: Present the henselization as a filtered colimit of localizations of etale algebras (proof lines 37545-37549).
Check each term is a valuation ring with the same value group and pass to the colimit (proof lines 37549-37561).
Repeat for the strict henselization and use the identification of the strict henselization of the henselization (proof lines 37562-37565).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a valuation ring the inclusions of its henselization and of its strict henselization are extensions of valuation rings inducing bijections on value groups, that is, they are weakly unramified (statement lines 37534-37543). The proof writes the henselization as a filtered colimit of localizations of etale algebras at primes over the maximal ideal, applies the statement about etale extensions of valuation rings to each term to get a valuation ring with the same value group, and then uses the statement about filtered colimits of valuation rings to conclude for the henselization; the strict henselization is treated by the same argument with the corresponding description, and the composite inclusion follows from the identification of the strict henselization of the henselization (proof lines 37545-37565). The colimit presentation and the two transfer statements are what make the argument uniform for both inclusions. The counted span refers four times, once to a result of this chapter and three times to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
